marketplace.name: guided-plugins
marketplace.description: Fourteen Claude Code plugins, one per classic software engineering book. Each ships 50+ skills, subagents and output styles built on the MIT-licensed rule sets from ciembor/agent-rules-books.

books.title: Clean Code
books.usefulWhen: Doing everyday coding and code review: naming, small functions, tests.

books.title: A Philosophy of Software Design
books.usefulWhen: Designing APIs or modules, or refactoring shallow abstractions.

books.title: Clean Architecture
books.usefulWhen: You need code that resists framework, database, and UI churn.

books.title: Code Complete
books.usefulWhen: You need disciplined implementation decisions on routines, control flow, and testing.

books.title: Designing Data-Intensive Applications
books.usefulWhen: Data ownership, event flows, or consistency semantics matter.

books.title: Domain-Driven Design
books.usefulWhen: You want to model the business domain rather than tables, controllers, or DTOs.

books.title: Domain-Driven Design Distilled
books.usefulWhen: You want DDD benefits without heavy ceremony.

books.title: Implementing Domain-Driven Design
books.usefulWhen: You need implementation-level DDD: aggregates, events, and integrations.

books.title: Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture
books.usefulWhen: You need to choose an appropriate enterprise pattern instead of mixing responsibilities.

books.title: Refactoring
books.usefulWhen: You want small, test-backed structural changes kept separate from feature work.

books.title: Refactoring.Guru
books.usefulWhen: You need to diagnose smells, pick a safe treatment, and avoid uncontrolled redesign.

books.title: Release It!
books.usefulWhen: You are building services, APIs, queues, or critical production paths.

books.title: The Pragmatic Programmer
books.usefulWhen: You want a general engineering layer: automation, feedback, orthogonality.

books.title: Working Effectively with Legacy Code
books.usefulWhen: You are changing poorly tested legacy code and need to regain control first.
